problem_fits.caveat: Conditional logic plus redirect on completion is a Tally-side path to answer-dependent routing, but nothing in the ledger states that the webhook endpoint's HTTP response is surfaced to the respondent; the only documented response.
problem_fits.why: Product material covers branching and post-submit redirect but not webhook-response control of the respondent's screen.
No ledger evidence describes how choice-field option values are represented in the webhook payload, so there is nothing positive to reference.

problem_fits.caveat: The licensed material gives a direct Airtable path and a way to inspect what Tally delivered and what the endpoint answered, but it documents nothing about field-level mapping behaviour, so a single field going missing on write still.
problem_fits.why: Delivery inspection plus a native Airtable route narrows where the fault sits without explaining the reported field loss.

problem_fits.caveat: Delivery events, retries and the failure email let the builder confirm whether Tally sent the submission at all, but retrying is documented only for failed attempts and nothing in the ledger re-delivers an already-successful submission.
problem_fits.why: Tally's delivery log separates a Tally-side failure from the automation platform's test semantics, but cannot change the latter.

problem_fits.caveat: reCAPTCHA covers bot spam, duplicate prevention covers repeat records, and email verification covers one field — but it is Business-plan only, and the ledger documents no check for typos or blank values in other fields, so the pass/fail.
problem_fits.why: Several named failure modes have licensed form-side checks; the validation gate as a whole does not.

segment_objections.objection: Webhooks are the part that always sits behind a paid plan, so this will cost us before we can even test it.
segment_objections.answer: Webhooks are free to all Tally users and the number of webhook URLs you can connect is not capped, and each can be paused with a toggle.

segment_objections.objection: Nobody owns this pipeline, so if a delivery fails we will find out weeks later from a missing record.
segment_objections.answer: Failed deliveries are retried after 5 minutes, 30 minutes, 1 hour, 6 hours and 1 day; if all retries fail, a one-time email goes to the form owner and creator with the reason and a link to fix it, and delivery events can be listed.

segment_objections.objection: How do I know a payload arriving at my endpoint actually came from the form and not from someone who found the URL?
segment_objections.answer: Tally can sign each request with a SHA256 signature carried in a Tally-Signature header, so the payload can be verified before it is processed.

segment_objections.objection: My scenario does more than a couple of seconds of work before it can answer.
segment_objections.answer: The endpoint has a documented 10-second timeout to process and respond, and longer work is expected to be handed to another service internally.

segment_objections.objection: 'Unlimited and free' always has a throttle hidden somewhere, and we will hit it.
segment_objections.answer: Unlimited forms and submissions are free subject to a stated fair-usage policy; the ledger names the policy but does not quantify its thresholds, so the ceiling cannot be stated here.

segment_objections.objection: We have no engineer, so anything that needs endpoints and JSON is not for us.
segment_objections.answer: Submissions can be synced without handling payloads yourself through the Zapier, Make, Pipedream and Integrately integrations, which are the documented non-technical route.
